newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy sees "satisfactory" trend in state accounts.
newsitem.headline: Italy sees "satisfactory" trend in state accounts.

text.p: Italian Treasury undersecretary Laura Pennachi said on Thursday that state finances were performing well in February after a surplus in January and the situation was "satisfactory".
"January's data were comforting, with a surplus in public accounts," Pennacchi told "World and Business" newspaper in an interview.
"The February acccounts are also going well and so we have a satisfactory situation," she said. Her remarks were confirmed by her spokesman.

Italy had a surplus of two trillion lire in January after a 12.29 trillion public sector borrowing requirement in January 1996. Analysts have forecast a PSBR of some 7.5-8.5 trillion lire in February, compared with a 12.971 trillion PSBR a year earlier.
